body: A compatible CSS update replaces the stylesheet while preserving running scripts\, so later mutations through a script\'s cached `style.sheet` reference no longer affect the displayed design\.

Fixed in `9b2d366`. The original `textContent` write recreated the stylesheet. Updates now splice rules on the existing `CSSStyleSheet`, preserving unchanged prefix/suffix rules and all rule objects for canonical no-ops. Separate physical-text and rendered-CSS baselines retain conflict detection across repeated updates, including styles without IDs.

The new regression reproduced the failure before the fix. All 17 preview browser tests now pass. The Next production build passes, and an 18-check Chrome probe against the built routes/updater confirms that a real click can still modify displayed CSS through the original cached sheet reference. Identity and stored data were simulated for that probe.

Resolved in 9b2d366\: compatible CSS updates now modify the existing stylesheet through CSSOM splices\, preserving cached `style.sheet` references across successive updates\. Regression coverage checks sheet identity\, visible mutations through the cached sheet\, anonymous stylesheets\, and subsequent conflict detection\.

Every screenshot capture on Upstash fails because the reply waiter sends BLPOP to the REST API\, which does not support blocking list commands\.
Pressing Back to the draft URL while an uncached history chat is opening leaves its request active\, so the late response displays that chat even though the URL no longer names it\.

Confirmed and fixed in 9e8a8e0: the popstate handler now treats a chat that is still opening as not being on a draft, so Back resets to the new chat and the late snapshot is dropped. Covered by a new UI test that failed before the fix.

Resolved in 9e8a8e0\: Back to the new\-chat page now cancels any pending chat selection\, preventing its late snapshot from replacing the draft\.

<!-- OMNIAGENT-REVIEW-RESOLUTION:a255cf6cd09f37f56867cf3f1182caf59bbaf54dfadf285cc79c85edda587308 -->

Navigating Back to a just\-deleted chat before its pending read finishes still displays the deleted content because the deletion guard prevents caching but does not reject the snapshot returned to the new selection\.

After a known failure\, polling never resumes a newly admitted message whose background invocation is lost\, because the room retains error status even though its pending input exceeds failed\_through\.
When the first style element has a nonmatching media query or a non\-CSS type\, embedded font faces inherit that restriction and disappear from previews and exports despite successful downloads\.
A transient font\-download failure produces a cacheable fallback preview whose revision\-only ETag prevents subsequent reloads from retrying the fonts after Google recovers\.

Fixed in 91460bc. Font faces now reuse only unconditional CSS styles (no restrictive media/non-CSS type/disabled/title); otherwise a new unconditional style is added without weakening the original style. Added a regression test that failed before the fix and a real-Chrome case covering restricted first styles, no eligible style, screenshots and offline export. A newly inserted style safely falls back to full reloads rather than hot updates. Browser suite: 43/43 pass.

Fixed in 91460bc. Font-bearing HTML previews now use private, no-store with no revision-only ETag, so an old If-None-Match cannot return an early 304 and freeze a fallback. The server-side font cache remains in use, and designs without fonts retain revision-based 304s. Added a regression test that first forces a font failure, then recovers at the same revision with the old validator: it failed with 304 before the fix and now reloads the font successfully. Auth/route suite: 276/276 pass.

Resolved in 91460bc\: embedded faces now use an unconditional CSS style element\, or a new one when no suitable element exists\.

Resolved in 91460bc\: font\-bearing previews no longer use revision\-only ETags\, so reloads can retry font preparation after a transient failure\.

<!-- OMNIAGENT-REVIEW-RESOLUTION:b3dc8f02ac154cedec5cc3d4db572513933236c685eeec0f71ec49f43919477f -->
When a delayed bootstrap publishes the predecessor of a pending rotation\, retrying the pending cookie adopts that already\-consumed token and discards its only live successor\.

Fixed in 2cf7239.

Pending publication now binds the token actually consumed as well as the predecessor's raw seal. A differently sealed copy of that consumed predecessor is repaired with CAS against the observed raw record. Recovery rereads and reclassifies after contention, permits at most two writes, and preserves the live pending successor if contention persists. Revocation fencing and the original retention deadline are unchanged.

Added a causal regression with one-hour provider tokens, plus coverage for resealing, CAS exhaustion and later recovery, a durable winner, revocation, and older pending-cookie formats. Older ambiguous metadata returns 503 with the credential preserved instead of guessing which token is newer.

Verification: 13 focused tests, `npm run test:auth` (322 passed), `npm run test:core` (199 passed), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check`; all final checks exited 0. Provider and Redis boundaries use synthetic responses.

Resolved in 2cf7239\: pending publication now identifies the consumed predecessor token and repairs a delayed or resealed bootstrap record with bounded CAS retries\, preserving the live successor on contention\.
